sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Exothermic Reaction Self-Heating Instant Meals

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-2 to L. 561-15 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) implementing EU AMLD5/6; Decree No. 2017-924 of 6 May 2017 on beneficial ownership transparency; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 on transparency, anti-corruption and economic modernisation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity card of UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority in country of origin
Competent local authority or utility provider

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and French domestic sanctions screening standards

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted for foreign names
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or similar to existing companies or reserved names
Words infringing public policy, morality or trademarks
Protected professional or ministerial designations without prior approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection notice; subsequent judicial review available

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for administrative registered office but must be verifiable and accessible; physical presence required for certain regulated activities
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10% for standard manufacturing pre-incorporation compliance checks)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, name reservation and incorporation filing fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for corporate formation
Market benchmark for beneficial ownership compliance services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Apostille office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fees for international document authentication

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-56 (SARL); general corporate provisions Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry) and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) electronic single window.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 business creation form (déclaration de création d'une société commerciale) filed via the INPI Guichet unique électronique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum for SARL; capital is freely determined in the articles but must be at least €1. Cash contributions must be fully paid in and temporarily deposited with a notary, bank, or Caisse des Dépôts before filing, and are released upon registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's report unless a legal exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the initial share capital of the SARL, set at [€X] in the articles, has been fully subscribed and paid up; the chairman reports the temporary deposit of cash contributions in accordance with French law. 2. That the registered office is fixed at [registered address], effective immediately, for all legal and administrative purposes. 3. That [Name], nationality [–], domiciled at [–], is appointed Manager (Gérant) for an indefinite term, with full powers to bind the company within the corporate purpose. 4. That authorization is granted to the Manager to complete all formalities, sign all documents, and publish required notices before the registry. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles and Legal Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or qualified legal counsel; final filing with INPI Guichet unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare final SARL articles, capital allocation, manager appointment clauses, registered office election, and compliance with mandatory French corporate law requirements. Include the M0 form and beneficial ownership declaration. Verify entity name availability and corporate purpose compatibility.
required_dossiers: Certified identification of shareholders and managers
Proof of domiciliation of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or INPI queries the draft, revise the relevant clauses promptly, correct inconsistencies, and resubmit through the single window within the prescribed cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Capital and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, Caisse des Dépôts, or notary as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the SARL en formation, deposit the full amount of subscribed cash capital, and obtain the depositary's attestation. This attestation is mandatory for registration and must be produced to the registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of shareholders
Company name and business purpose outline
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening, select an alternative French financial institution or use a notary escrow; ensure the attestation states the depositary, amount, and holding conditions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique électronique (National Institute for Industrial Property).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed statuts, M0 form, proof of capital deposit, beneficial owner declaration, and any required notarized documents. Pay the filing and registration fees. A submission receipt with case number is issued immediately.
required_dossiers: Bank or notary capital deposit attestation
Copy of registered office lease or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by INPI or the registry, rectify missing or inconsistent information within the 15-day cure period; otherwise the file is forfeited and a new filing fee becomes payable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce of the competent jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The commercial registry verifies legality and compliance, registers the SARL in the RCS, issues the SIREN number, and generates the official registration document known as Extrait Kbis. This step establishes legal existence.
required_dossiers: INPI filing receipt and case file
Declaration of non-pending insolvency and criminal record statement as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a refusal, obtain the written reasons, remedy deficiencies through an amendment or supplemental document, and reapply; an appeal is possible before the president of the commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcements journal (JAL) and URSSAF, tax and INSEE registration portals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a legal notice of incorporation in an authorized legal gazette in the department of the registered office. Enroll the company with URSSAF for social security obligations and with the tax administration for corporate income tax and VAT; obtain SIRET establishment registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If enrollment is rejected, verify that the SIREN, corporate details, and legal form match the RCS data and resubmit corrected information; respond to any repeated query within the statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) and Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF), acting under the French Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Sanitary approval (agrément sanitaire) of the food establishment for self-heating instant meals, or registration as a food business operator under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004; additional operational authorization under the ICPE regime.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified installation under Rubrique 2220 (food preparation or manufacturing) of the French ICPE nomenclature, typically subject to the registration (enregistrement) regime; a full environmental impact assessment may be required if the production capacity exceeds the applicable high thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental discharge limits: chemical oxygen demand ≤ 125 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) ≤ 30 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 6.5–8.5; VOC and odor emissions require capture and treatment equipment; wastewater from exothermic production processes must be pretreated and waste solids handled under regulated waste management obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (avis de la commission de sécurité) for industrial premises; structural load inspection and building safety review by an approved technical control bureau; workplace occupational health assessment and clearance from CARSAT (health insurance fund for work accidents); compulsory first aid, evacuation signage, and training certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal and the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Business formation and initial registration data are filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); INSEE issues the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, while DGFiP assigns or confirms the French VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the SARL through the INPI Guichet unique and obtain the SIREN and SIRET numbers. 2. File the establishment, activity, registered office, directors, beneficial owners, and tax options with the competent SIE. 3. Request VAT registration or confirmation through the SIE or the impots.gouv.fr professional account, identifying the taxable activities, expected turnover, commencement date, bank details, and applicable VAT regime. 4. Obtain the French VAT number in the format FR plus a two-digit validation key and the entity's nine-digit SIREN. 5. Obtain an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number from French customs before importing or exporting goods. 6. Non-EU established businesses making taxable supplies in France generally require French VAT registration and may need an accredited French fiscal representative, subject to applicable treaty or reciprocity rules; EU-established businesses generally do not require a fiscal representative. 7. Maintain the SIREN, SIRET, VAT number, EORI number, tax correspondence, VAT returns, invoices, customs records, and evidence of business establishment. A foreign entity without a French establishment must register when it makes French-taxable transactions for which it is liable to account for French VAT, subject to reverse-charge rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying SARL may elect for income-tax transparency (impôt sur le revenu, IR), including a family SARL election where all qualifying shareholders are members of the same qualifying family group. A SARL incorporated for fewer than five years may elect for IR for a maximum five-year period if statutory conditions are satisfied, including size, ownership, activity, and capital requirements. France has no general US-style check-the-box election and no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification mechanism. Anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU ATAD 2 framework and can deny deductions, impose income inclusions, or restrict relief where relevant cross-border hybrid arrangements exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the French General Tax Code and EU VAT Directive framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no universal VAT registration threshold for ordinary taxable businesses: VAT registration and liability generally arise from the first taxable transaction for which the business is responsible for French VAT. The franchise en base de TVA may exempt qualifying small businesses below applicable turnover limits, generally EUR 85,000 for goods, food, and accommodation activities and EUR 37,500 for services, with increased thresholds generally applicable at EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively, subject to the rules and transitional provisions in force for the relevant tax year. Businesses exceeding the applicable thresholds must transition to an actual VAT regime. Intra-EU acquisitions, imports, distance sales, domestic reverse-charge transactions, and other special regimes may trigger registration independently of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France currently does not operate a universal real-time VAT invoice clearance system for ordinary private-sector transactions, and there is no general requirement for a government digital stamp on every invoice. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for transactions with French public-sector bodies through Chorus Pro. The private-sector reform requires all businesses established in France to be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuing obligations are scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory implementation and transitional rules. In-scope domestic B2B invoices must generally be transmitted through an approved Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP), with structured invoice data transmitted to the administration. B2C and cross-border transaction data is generally subject to electronic reporting rather than domestic B2B invoice transmission. Required data fields include supplier and customer identification, VAT numbers where applicable, transaction amounts, VAT rates, payment terms, and transaction category. Businesses must retain electronically issued and received invoices in an auditable form for the statutory retention period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union are generally exempt from French VAT under the export exemption rules, functionally equivalent to zero-rating, where the goods leave the EU customs territory and the supplier retains legally sufficient proof of export and supplier involvement in the dispatch. Typical evidence includes the electronic export declaration, MRN, customs exit confirmation, transport documents, commercial invoice, packing list, and proof linking the goods to the transaction. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is identified for VAT in another Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and transport from France to that Member State is substantiated. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is foreign. B2B services are generally outside French VAT under the customer-location rule and require reverse charge by the customer; B2C services and special-category services follow separate place-of-supply rules. Export exemption or non-taxation must be supported by customer status, place of supply, transport, customs, and accounting evidence. Input VAT refunds may be claimed through periodic French VAT returns or, for eligible non-established businesses, applicable EU or non-EU refund procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU export customs declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the French supplier, customer, goods, values, Incoterms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and product description sufficient to reconcile the shipment with the invoice
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or other transport evidence
Evidence of delivery or receipt outside the European Union where available
EORI number and customs representation records
Purchase order, sales contract, shipping instructions, and accounting reconciliation
Evidence of payment where relevant to establish the transaction and reconcile proceeds; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French export-VAT document
For intra-EU supplies: customer VAT identification number, recapitulative statement evidence, and proof of transport to the other Member State
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to export proceeds and no general 180-day repatriation requirement. Export VAT exemption may be reassessed where customs exit, transport, customer, invoice, accounting, or transaction-linkage evidence is missing, inconsistent, fabricated, or not retained. The reassessment can include the VAT that should have been collected, statutory late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month under Article 1727 of the French General Tax Code, and applicable procedural or payment penalties. Deliberate or materially abusive conduct may attract a 40% penalty for deliberate failure, an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, and potentially criminal tax-fraud sanctions, including imprisonment and substantial fines. Incorrect input-VAT refunds may be clawed back with interest and penalties. Customs violations may additionally trigger customs duties, import VAT, administrative penalties, seizure, or other sanctions. The taxpayer bears the burden of maintaining an auditable evidentiary chain linking the exported goods, customs exit, invoice, accounting records, and applicable VAT treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority); Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances, acts as the competent authority for cross-border capital-movement regulations and international financial sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a eurozone member and the euro is fully convertible. Article 63 TFEU guarantees free movement of capital and payments within the EU and with third countries, subject to EU-wide safeguards. Both current-account transfers (trade, services, royalties, salaries) and capital-account operations (equity subscription, shareholder loans, dividend remittances, liquidation proceeds) are permitted without exchange-control authorization. Practical hurdles for profit remittance from a French SARL are: compliance with French company-law solvency and dividend-distribution rules, preparation of approved financial statements, anti-money-laundering source-of-funds controls by the paying bank, possible withholding-tax relief procedures when dividends are paid to non-resident shareholders, and periodic statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the Banque de France for cross-border direct-investment flows above reportable thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no EU or French statutory requirements to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no deadline for converting foreign currency into euros. A French exporter may retain foreign-currency receivables in a foreign-currencybank account or freely sell them on the interbank market. The practical compliance burden consists of customs valuation and Intrastat/EXTRASTAT reporting for goods movements, balance-of-payments declaration duties for settlement with non-residents when triggered, anti-money-laundering transaction documentation, and the corporate requirement to record and tax realized foreign-exchange gains or losses. No export proceeds need to be repatriated to France within any specified window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de séquestre) and Euro Commercial Operating Account
Corporate Current Account and Designated Capital Subscription Account
Operational Corporate Account and Trade-Finance Facility Account
Current Account, Import Letter-of-Credit Sub-Limit, and FX Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary disbursement channel, Low as a primary treasury rail. Legal constraints: a non-French electronic-money institution (EMI) must be authorized or validly passported under the Second Electronic Money Directive and PSD2 to issue e-money or provide payment services in France. Offshore and non-EU EMIs generally cannot lawfully provide French IBANs or hold French escrow funds without a licensed branch, a partner-banking sponsor, or another compliant local structure. A SARL may use an EU/EEA-authorized EMI for sales-collection convenience and low-value outbound payments, but inbound equity capital, commercial-letter-of-credit issuance, high-value trade settlements, and any bank-confirmed hedging lines must be run through a Tier-1 French credit institution to mitigate clearing, segregation, and regulatory risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French monetary and financial law does not impose an absolute statutory requirement that all SARL directors appear physically at a bank branch, but in practice most Tier-1 French banks require an in-person meeting with the manager and ultimate beneficial owners when the entity is newly incorporated, foreign-owned, or starting a cross-border trade model. Remote opening can be approved on a case-by-case basis using eIDAS-compliant electronic signatures, video-identification procedures, and apostilled or certified document packages, particularly for EU-resident directors. For non-EU directors, a physical KYC interview at a French branch or at a correspondent bank/embassy-consular office is frequently mandated, and the bank may also require original signature cards to be wet-signed at the first board meeting in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated French SARL with 100% non-resident LLC ownership, no French credit history, and a high initial paid-in capital relative to start-up activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association, updated Kbis extract, UBO declaration form, ownership diagram, signed board resolutions, parent-company audited financial statements for the last two years, banker's references, six-month source-of-funds statements for the capital contribution, detailed business plan for the self-heating instant-water-pot manufacturing and distribution model, tax residence certificates, and a French corporate-law counsel opinion confirming legality of the capital structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry classification involving exothermic self-heating chemistry, food-grade instant meals, and imported chemical heating components, triggering product-safety and trade-compliance review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGCCRF food-business-operator registration or relevant sectoral license, sanitary or product-safety certificates, UN classification and safety data sheets for the heating exothermic compound, ADR/IATA transport-classification reports, CE or applicable EU conformity declarations, third-party laboratory test reports, production and traceability SOPs, import/export customs records, and product-liability insurance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection or cross-border supplier payments involving counterparties located in non-EU jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering or sanctions concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts, invoices, bills of lading and customs declarations, full SWIFT payment confirmations from the sending bank, twelve-month bank statements of all material counterparties, corporate registration and VAT/tax-residence evidence, UBO declarations from the counterparty, end-user and anti-sanctions certificates, and a group-wide AML/CFT compliance letter from the parent organization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or SARL manager appears on PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlists, or source of wealth cannot be explained from salary, dividends, asset sales, or ordinary business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid government-issued identity documents, PEP-status narrative and declaration, detailed wealth-and-source-of-funds history, asset sale contracts, inheritance instruments, bank and brokerage statements, tax-residence certificates and tax-clearance documents, professional reference letters, independent legal counsel opinion, and a clean negative-media report prepared by a reputable screening provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital must be settled by a high-quality wire transfer from the non-resident parent or subscriber to the French SARL's segregated capital-subscription bank account using the beneficiary IBAN and BIC. The remitting bank must transmit an MT103 with a clear reference in the remittance-information field identifying the transaction as an 'apport en capital' or paid-in capital contribution. Use the ISO 20022 External Purpose Code 'CAPC' for a capital increase, the bank-specific code for equity injection if required by the French balance-of-payments survey, or 'LOAN' for a shareholder loan. No exchange-control approval is required for an inbound EUR remittance, but the first transfer may be quarantined pending full AML/source-of-funds clearance. The SARL must file the applicable direct-investment declaration with the Banque de France (or through its bank) where the transaction threshold or reporting regime applies, and must retain the capital-subscription deed, updated shareholding register, board resolutions, identity documents, bank reference letters, and proof of the upstream corporate chain to satisfy both French bank compliance and anti-money-laundering verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement should use the most cost-efficient and compliant rail based on beneficiary jurisdiction: SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA Credit Transfer with IBAN for European suppliers; SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA cross-border wire transfers; and irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit under UCP600 for high-value imports such as chemical heating cores, insulated aluminium bodies, food-grade packaging, and assembly-equipment purchases. Documentary collections under URC522 may be used for trusted ongoing suppliers. Each payment file must contain the correct ISO purpose code for trade in goods, invoice and packing-list cross-references, Incoterms, customs tariff classification, country-of-origin evidence, and any required import/export documentation. Correspondent-bank fees, jurisdiction-specific sanctions checks, and currency-clearing constraints must be validated before final transaction release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in euro against the trade settlement currency, supported by a genuine underlying commercial exposure, documented under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank long-form FX confirmation, and subject to EMIR trade-reporting and margin obligations if applicable.

FX swaps and swap-like rollover/extension transactions with the same underlying commercial exposure, used to match intercompany dividend or import-payment cash-flow dates, subject to counterparty credit approval and internal treasury policies.

Plain-vanilla European currency options purchased by the SARL to hedge euro/non-euro receivables or payables, including EUR/USD and EUR/CNH structures, where the option premium reflects only hedge cost and no speculative uncovered writing.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid, restricted, or non-deliverable emerging-market currencies, executed only when a valid underlying transaction requires settlement in a currency that cannot be delivered by conventional clearing rules, and documented under an ISDA-compliant NDF confirmation with EMIR reporting retained.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for SMEs on first €42,500 profit; additional 10% reduced rate for profits up to €50,000 for certain small businesses; tax credit for research (CIR) and innovation (CII) may apply; participation exemption for qualifying subsidiaries (95% exemption on dividends received).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (income tax return) and annexes (2058-A to 2058-G) filed via the French tax authority's online portal (impots.gouv.fr) or through the EDI (Échange de Données Informatisé) system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending December 31, the return must be filed by the second business day after May 1st of the following year. For other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (or loss) after adjustments for tax deductions and add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a permanent establishment in France must report French-source income in this box; otherwise, file a limited return for withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net long-term capital gains subject to reduced rate (currently 15% for certain assets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains from disposal of French real estate or shares in French real estate companies; may be subject to specific withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., research tax credit, family tax credit) to be offset against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim credits only if they have a permanent establishment in France and the credit is attributable to that PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions (e.g., for investments in overseas territories) that reduce the tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally not available to non-residents unless the activity is carried out through a French PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after all adjustments, used to compute the corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, this box reflects the taxable income attributable to the French PE; if no PE, the return is limited to withholding tax obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due if filed within 30 days of the deadline; 40% if filed after 30 days; 80% if the return is fraudulent. Interest on late payment: 0.20% per month. Additional penalties for failure to file annexes: €150 per missing document.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (domestic law) for dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% for individuals (flat tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the beneficial owner must provide a certificate of tax residence (Formulaire 5000) to the paying entity before the payment. The French tax authority may require a prior approval (rescrit fiscal) for certain treaty benefits. The payer must retain the certificate and supporting documentation for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (domestic law), reduced to 0% under most treaties (e.g., EU Interest and Royalties Directive) if the beneficial owner is an EU company. Interest: statutory 30% (domestic law), reduced to 0% under most treaties (EU directive) for related parties. Treaty rates vary; typical range 0-15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is required if the French entity or group has annual turnover or total assets exceeding €400 million, or if the group's consolidated turnover exceeds €400 million. For smaller entities, a simplified documentation (form 2257) is required if the entity has related-party transactions exceeding €50,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the 'substance over form' doctrine and anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155-A of the French Tax Code) to prevent artificial arrangements. While there is no specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) as in offshore jurisdictions, French tax authorities scrutinize the actual business activity, decision-making, and operational substance of entities claiming tax benefits. A French SARL must demonstrate real economic presence (employees, premises, business functions) to avoid challenges under the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) and to benefit from treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of transactions to avoid corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: up to €500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for individuals; corporate fine up to €1,000,000. Civil penalties: 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed serious misconduct (e.g., fraud, misappropriation). They may face civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment (up to 5 years).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SARL with no real economic activity, solely to obtain tax advantages or to channel funds without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the entity and reattribute income to the actual beneficial owner. Penalties: 80% of the tax due for abuse of law (abus de droit), plus interest. Criminal sanctions for money laundering if applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the tax debts of the shell company if they acted in bad faith. They may face criminal prosecution for tax fraud and money laundering, leading to imprisonment and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., customer due diligence, reporting of suspicious transactions) when engaging in cash-intensive or high-risk activities, or when dealing with sanctioned entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 5% of turnover for legal entities; criminal penalties for directors up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for AML breaches, including civil damages and criminal sanctions. They may face travel bans and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for lack of documentation, and interest. In cases of serious mispricing, a 80% penalty may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the tax adjustment if they knowingly approved the mispricing. They may face civil liability for damages to the company and criminal charges for tax evasion.
